newsitem.title: USA: Hughes signs satellite launch deal with Japanese firm.
newsitem.headline: Hughes signs satellite launch deal with Japanese firm.

text.p: Hughes Space and Communications International Inc. said Tuesday it signed a contract with Rocket System Corp. of Japan for at least 10 satellite launches on the private Japanese company's new H-IIA rocket for an unspecified price.
The deal is part of the U.S. satellite maker's efforts to lower the costs of launching spacecraft by widening competition in the industry.

Hughes, a unit of Hughes Electronics Corp., which is a subsidiary of General Motors Corp., said in a statement that the 10 launches would take place over a five-year period beginning in the year 2000.
The company did not disclose the financial terms of the contract, but said it included an undisclosed number of options for more launches.
The Wall Street Journal Tuesday quoted a senior company official as saying that the services and options were worth about $1 billion.
Hughes said in a statement the launches would be available to its customers as well as any Hughes Electronics business unit.
"This contract deepens our long-term commitment to support the communications needs of Japan, today and into the 21st century," it said.
Rocket System is a private company formed with investors from more than 70 Japanese companies to commercially market the H-IIA launch vehicle.

The H-IIA is Japan's newest entry into the intermediate-lift launch vehicle market, designed specifically to carry international commercial payloads to geosynchronous orbit, where a satellite appears to remain over a fixed point on Earth.
Hughes said the H-IIA rocket is capable of lifting Hughes' two largest satellite models, which weigh between 3 tons and 5 tons at launch.
The rockets will lift off from a launch site in Tanegashima, Japan.
